items.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09
items.q: Don Ellis, Blood, Sweat, and Tears is a reasonably big band.

ctx.x: Well, I think I'd like to see them come back. I really would, but... I think it's on the way. You think they really ever went? Well, I mean, to keep a band intact now, with the cost of keeping a band up of any size. It's a salary that you have to pay. And you can't find many places that will pay the money. Vegas is making us, I think, making a big effort to bring back. Right, they're the only Buddy Rich, you know, has... Big bands. There's a lot of big bands. But that's the only place they can work. They can work…

Buddy's band has been working some of the rock places, though, like Fillmore East and Fillmore West. And the kids are dancing to big bands. Don Ellis, Blood, Sweat, and Tears is a reasonably big band.
That's right. Look, about... Say, my band is up to nine to ten pieces. But it's pretty big.
